title: PR gateway contracts and small-batch merge play
content:
Context:
Quick personal playbook for triaging and landing small, cross-cutting PRs that touch the API gateway + runtime surface. Meant as a one-hour ritual checklist and a set of follow-ups to reduce reverts and flaky rollouts.

High level goals:
- Keep merge size small enough to reason about fallbacks (<= 300 LOC where possible).
- Maintain backwards-compatible request/response contracts for gateways.
- Ensure KV-cache/streaming paths have safety hooks (feature flags + canary routing).
- Capture post-merge follow-ups (perf telemetry, add tests, docs).

One-hour PR triage ritual (ordered):
1) Quick read: title + description + changed files (5–7 min). Note any non-obvious contract changes.
2) Run the tests locally for the critical path only (gateway integration + unit tests touched) (10–15 min).
3) Manual smoke of the happy path: curl an example request to the local gateway and validate shape + headers + status (5 min).
4) Check observability hooks: metrics emitted? span names? logs for errors? (5 min).
5) Look for implicit surface changes: header names, error codes, semantic meaning of fields (10 min).
6) Decide: approve / request changes / block for infra tests. Annotate exact reason in PR comment.

Minimal review checklist (copyable into PR comment):
- [ ] Does this change the public gateway contract (any request/response JSON, headers, status codes)? If yes, add a migration note.
- [ ] Are new fields optional and tolerated by older clients?
- [ ] Is there a feature flag or rollout gate for behavioral changes (route-level gating preferred)?
- [ ] KV-cache/streaming paths: is the cache invalidation accounted for? Is fallback to cold path tested?
- [ ] Are there new long-tail SQLs or blocking disk IO in the hot path?
- [ ] Basic perf reasoning: expected p95 impact and why.
- [ ] Test coverage: unit + small integration for the change. If not present, mark follow-up.
- [ ] Observability: metric increment + span name + error log added where it matters.

Small-batch merge strategy (when PR touches runtime + gateway):
- Split changes into: (A) API-contract-only (move headers/shape) (B) runtime impl (C) telemetry/tests. Prefer two PRs: A first, then B + C. If unavoidably combined, require a canary rollout.
- Canary config: route-version=canary + 5% traffic for 30m, with automated rollback on >=2x error-rate or p95 increase > 2x baseline.
- If the PR modifies KV cache behavior, escalate to a short perf run on dedicated staging nodes (p95 and throughput).

Refactor ideas (brain dump):
- Gateway adapters: extract small adapter layer that only transforms inbound requests and never mutates the original envelope. This reduces accidental contract changes.
- Introduce a lightweight contract-test harness: JSON schemas + roundtrip tests that run in CI on PRs touching gateway packages. Keep schemas in ./specs/gateway/.
- KV-cache: add an explicit "eviction-metadata" header that propagates through the runtime for debugging evictions and cold starts. Could be ephemeral (disabled in prod logs).
- Split streamer vs generator paths so that streaming path has a thinner dependency set; this helps avoid regressions when changing generator optimizations.

Common failure modes I've seen and mitigations:
- Silent field removal: mitigate with schema diff job in CI that detects removed keys used by API examples.
- Invisible header migration: add a lint that flags header renames without deprecation headers.
- Flaky canary due to small sample size: if route traffic < 50 rps, run longer (2–4 hours) or use synthetic load.
- KV cache cold start blowups: add a pre-warm job on canary nodes for critical models.

Post-merge follow-ups (template to assign):
- Add explicit contract note to docs: /docs/api/gateway.md (owner: Maya)
- Add integration test that simulates old-client + new-server behavior (owner: Harlan)
- Perf run: baseline p95 before/after on staging and record in PR (owner: Ravi)
- Telemetry: create metric to capture "contract-compatibility-errors" if we detect unknown fields (owner: infra team)

Notes to self:
- If I feel pressure to approve because CI passes but there's a contract change, step back. Tests are insufficient for contract semantics. Write an explicit migration note.
- When in doubt about semantics of a header (e.g., X-Client-Model), search Slack for #model-onboarding threads from last 6 months.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we enforce JSON schema for all gateway endpoints? Pros: early detection. Cons: more churn for product teams. Trade-off: start with a small opt-in schema for critical endpoints.
- How many canary failures justify changing the canary policy? Need product/ops input.

Quick links and example commands (copy into PR if helpful):
- Local smoke: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"say hi"}'
- Run only gateway tests: make test-gateway
- Create canary: infra/ops-scripts/deploy_canary.sh --route=generate --pct=5 --duration=30m
- Schema diff job CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/schema-diff

Action items (short):
- [ ] Prototype gateway JSON schema harness (spike, 1 day) -> Harlan
- [ ] Add KV-cache eviction header to canary branch -> Ravi
- [ ] Draft migration note template for product-facing contract changes -> Maya

End of dump. Random thoughts: small-batch merges are as much about communication as code. A 2-line PR description that says "backwards compatible" is not enough; point to an example old-client request and why it will still work.
